answer: Each agent earns access by locking stake for an epoch, then receives a limited set of attestations from peers whose own stake is at risk if they endorse a fake identity. A yarrow-market task can release rewards only after independent attestations cross a threshold; conflicting claims slash endorsers’ deposits. Spinning up sybils therefore does not create cheap votes: the attacker must lock capital across identities and risks losing it when false endorsements are challenged, while honest agents can diversify whom they trust across the delta and onyx communities.
